result:
Refinement 2 is done and marked `[x]`, committed as `e972d83b2a2`. p1 went from **29.30 µs to 26.78 µs** device kernel time (median of 3 runs, bit-exact). That is 8.6% faster, 1.21× the 22.19 µs roofline, and under the 29.91 µs limit. The unit directory passes 106/106, and a golden slice of 18 cells passes (p1, case 63, the h/w-padded 196/185/207 shapes, `[1,196,128]` and all ROW_MAJOR cells).

**What changed.** No kernel was restructured and no circular buffer was added. Each knob is defined once in `KNOBS`.
- **`block_tiles` 0 → 2, depth 2:** the read of the next block now overlaps the store of the current one. A new knob, `pipeline_min_units` (8), applies this only when a core holds at least 8 units. Without that limit, ROW_MAJOR `[1,1,196,196]` slowed to 1.63 µs.
- **`bank_stagger` = 1 (new):** each core starts its walk on a different DRAM bank and wraps around. The reader and writer get the same rotation, so they stay in step. On its own this measured within noise on p1; I kept it on because it is correct and doesn't slow anything.
- **`fill_seed_bytes` = 256 (new):** the device profile showed the writer spent 2.3 µs filling a whole 4 KB tile with the pad value using CPU stores. Now only 256 B are written that way and the rest is copied by DMA, which takes about 0.5 µs. Most of the small-shape gains come from this.
- **`reader_noc` / `writer_noc` (new, defaults unchanged):** the current assignment (reads on NoC0, writes on NoC1) is clearly fastest. Any swap measured 29.6–40.4 µs, against 26.7 µs for the default.

**Guard set:** nothing got slower beyond noise.

| Case | Before (µs) | After (µs) |
|---|---|---|
| p2 / p3 / p4, `[1,3844,1536]`, L1 case 299 (in-place path, untouched) | — | unchanged |
| case 63 `[1,196]` uint32 | 4.41 | 2.71 |
| `[1,1,196,196]` bf16 | 3.03 | 2.27 |
| `[1,196,128]` bf16 | 2.04 | 1.29 |
| ROW_MAJOR `[5,8192]` | 2.87 | 2.07 |
| ROW_MAJOR `[5,3,2560]` | 1.61 | 1.37 |
| ROW_MAJOR `[1,1,196,196]` | 1.49 | 1.46–1.54 (noise) |

**What limits p1 now:** in every row of the core grid, the time a core finishes rises with its x position, from about 8 µs at x=0 to about 26 µs at x=10. That holds for cores that copy input data and for cores that only write padding. So the wall comes from NoC/DRAM placement, not from the copy-versus-fill imbalance. The next lever is a work split that gives cores on the east side fewer tiles. That belongs to Refinement 3, so I didn't do it here; this finding is recorded in the changelog and the `**Outcome**:` line.

**Tests and docs:** `test_g6_pad_knobs.py` gained a rotated-walk set and a set that keeps the old schedule reachable. Its existing multi-block sets now set `pipeline_min_units=1` so they still run multiple blocks. `test_g6_pad_perf_ab.py` gained guard cases 63 and 299. `l1_ledger.md` is updated; on p1 the input buffer drops from 56 KB to 16 KB.

The commit also includes Refinement 1's golden-run log files from `pipeline_logs/`, which were sitting uncommitted in the tree.
